sections.html:
Caroline County lies in eastern Virginia, bounded on the north by the Rappahannock River. Richmond is about 30 miles to the south and Fredericksburg about 32 miles to the north, which puts the county between two job centers. The 2020 census counted 30,887 residents on 537 square miles, roughly twice the figure from fifty years before, so a lot of the housing is newer construction mixed into old farm country.

The county seat, Bowling Green, is also its largest town, and Port Royal is the only other incorporated one. A good share of residents work outside the county. Interstate 95 passes through with exits 104 and 110, and U.S. Routes 1, 17 and 301 cross the county as well. When buyers look at a Caroline house they weigh the drive along I-95 almost as much as the lot, and a property near an exit is easier to market than one down a long rural lane.

Caroline bills in two parts. A late payment picks up penalty and interest the next day, and personal property and business personal property follow the same calendar.

InstallmentDue datePenalty and interest added
First halfJune 5June 6: 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest
Second halfDecember 5December 6: 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest

State law draws the outer boundaries. Code of Virginia 58.1-3916 lets a locality charge up to 10 percent a year in interest and up to 10 percent of the overdue tax as a penalty. A locality may waive both if the lateness was not the taxpayer's doing, or if a timely mailed payment carried proof of mailing and showed up within five days of the deadline.

sections.h2: Who to call: Treasurer and Commissioner
sections.html:
Your tax runs through two desks. Payments go to the Treasurer, and the Commissioner of the Revenue deals with assessment questions.

  • Treasurer: 212 N Main Street, Bowling Green, VA 22427, 804-633-5291, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Payments by mail go to P.O. Box 431.
  • Commissioner's real estate office: 804-633-9834 or realestate@co.caroline.va.us.
  • General county mail: P.O. Box 447, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

You can pay online, by phone through ACI, by mail, at the office window, or through monthly automatic withdrawal. After hours, use the drop box in front of the County Administration Building. The county stands behind only the payments made through its own website and Official Payments. If you send money through your bank's bill-pay service and it goes astray, the loss is yours.

sections.h2: How to check or appeal your assessment
sections.html:
Look up your parcel in the Real Estate Assessment Information tool at caroline.civ.quest or on the Tax Map page, then call the Commissioner's real estate office. If that does not settle it, the Board of Equalization is next.

In a reassessment year, concerned owners are heard first by the Board of Assessors. A Board of Equalization is then seated for complaints. It has six citizen members who are nominated by the Board of Supervisors, approved by a Circuit Court judge and trained through the state tax department. Once it rules, the final route is a petition to Circuit Court under Section 58.1-3984.

Know the burden before you file. Section 58.1-3379 assumes the assessor got it right, so you must prove the value exceeds fair market value, was applied unevenly, or was set outside accepted appraisal practice. For a home with fewer than four units, a written request for the assessment records must be answered within 15 days.

Some pre-listing items sit with other offices.

  • Building permits. New construction, renovation, additions and major improvements all need one, along with plumbing and mechanical permits. A certificate of occupancy follows satisfactory completion. Building Inspections answers at 804-633-4303. Clear up any unpermitted work before you list.
  • Land use. The Commissioner of the Revenue runs the land preservation program and reviews each enrolled parcel every year. If yours is enrolled, ask that office about the effect of a sale.
  • Water. The county names the Carmel Church Ladysmith, Milford, Port Royal and Townfield systems. Public Utilities is at 804-633-4390.
  • Senior and disability relief. Call the real estate office at 804-633-9834.

On the deed, the grantor tax in 58.1-802 is 50 cents per $500 of value. The statute assigns it to the seller, and the two sides can agree to shift it.

Miss December 5 and the balance grows by December 6, when penalty and interest are added. The payoff at closing ends up bigger than the original bill.

Request the balance for your expected closing date and have the closing agent verify it. Proceeds cover the open amount. When repairs would scare off an ordinary buyer, an as-is purchase spares you the fix-up and the showings.

Cash Home Buyers will consider a Caroline County house that has back taxes. Your payoff comes from the Treasurer, and our offer can be built around that number.

A standard listing in Caroline County usually means permit cleanup, repairs, photos, showings and a wait for the buyer's lender. A direct as-is sale cuts most of that. You still owe the same tax, and the Treasurer's payoff is still the number that matters, but you are not paying carrying costs while the house sits on the market. Each month of waiting also adds to the risk of a missed bill, since penalty and interest arrive the day after a due date.

If you want to compare routes, ask an agent for a net-proceeds estimate and ask us for a written offer. Set both against the Treasurer's payoff and decide which leaves you better off.

sections.h2: A short checklist before you sell
sections.html:
Ring the Treasurer at 804-633-5291 for a payoff and the paid-installment history. Reach the real estate office at 804-633-9834 if the assessment seems off or you want the parcel records. Walk through the house looking for open permits or half-finished work, since a buyer's inspector or lender may ask about them. If the land sits in the preservation program, ask the Commissioner's office how a sale affects it.

Give your closing agent the written payoff plus the split you agreed for this year. The balance is then taken from your proceeds when the deed is recorded.

If you are a senior or have a disability, check whether the relief program reduces what a buyer will owe. That can change a buyer's calculation of the yearly cost, and the real estate office is the place to ask about it.

faqs.q: What are the Caroline County tax due dates?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. Penalty and interest of 10 percent each begin the following day.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Caroline County Treasurer?
faqs.a: Visit 212 N Main Street in Bowling Green on weekdays between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., call 804-633-5291, or write to P.O. Box 431, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

faqs.q: What is the appeal process for a Caroline County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Commissioner's real estate office, take any unresolved dispute to the Board of Equalization, and as a last resort petition Circuit Court under Section 58.1-3984.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I owe back taxes in Caroline County?
faqs.a: Usually. The open balance is paid from your proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer and have the closing agent double-check it.

faqs.q: Who owes the grantor tax at a Caroline County closing?
faqs.a: The seller, by default, at 50 cents per $500. Buyer and seller can agree that the buyer covers some or all of it.
